name: The Great Refactoring
description: Writing about video games from The Great Refactoring

name: The Greatest Games You (Probably) Never Played
description: Sean J. Jordan researches overlooked video games from early PC, arcade, and console eras, revisiting them to assess their merits beyond nostalgia. The publication spotlights games that were overlooked, misjudged, or confined to particular markets.

name: The Indie Games Round-up
description: Your ultimate indie game round-up! Each day's indie game releases, from big names to under-the radar gems, for consoles + PC, PLUS all the indie game announcements, reveals, and news from the week, for gamers + devs.

name: The Indie Informer
description: The Indie Informer is an independent games publication focused on indie titles, with news, reviews, features, and coverage of events and developers.

name: The Ludologist
description: My name is Jesper Juul, and I am a Ludologist [researcher of the design, meaning, culture, and politics of games]. This is my blog on game research and other important things.

name: The Magnificent 7s
description: Juliano Zucareli writes about games rated in the middle rather than the usual best-or-worst lists, highlighting the enjoyable or inventive qualities of overlooked titles.

name: The Nosy Gamer
description: The Nosy Gamer publishes commentary and analysis on online games, especially MMOs, their communities, and the businesses behind them. The feed's topic labels span games including EVE Online, Final Fantasy XIV, and World of Warcraft, as well as game-business issues.

name: The Pause Menu
description: The Pause Menu is a reflective gaming newsletter about games people return to and how games intersect with time, identity, and everyday life. Essays consider game mechanics and stories alongside their personal meaning.

name: The Phoenix Project
description: Book review site?

name: The Platform Layer
description: Petros Bountis examines gaming platforms such as Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo, and PC as systems, focusing on strategy, ecosystem dynamics, access models, and business incentives rather than console-cycle scorekeeping.

name: The Play Well Project
description: Writing about video games from The Play Well Project

name: The Postmode Newsletter
description: The Postmode Newsletter is Jordan Oloman's email publication with game reviews, interviews, and internet-culture analysis. It is presented as the newsletter arm of the independent Postmode site.

name: The PrinceWatercress Blog
description: The PrinceWatercress Blog publishes detailed video-game playthroughs and walkthrough guidance, explaining level progression, controls, enemies, and objectives across console and PC games.

name: The Rosetta String
description: The Rosetta String examines video-game localization, including linguistic and cultural translation, interface constraints, localization quality assurance, and technical workflows. Its author describes the work as aimed at linguists, localization professionals, and game developers.

name: The Saved Game
description: The Saved Game is Joe's gaming publication about discovering or revisiting games old and new. Its articles include personal perspectives, game history, the people behind games, and research-based news.

name: The Solo Gamedev
description: The Solo Gamedev shares Mariusz's experience learning and making video games, with advice and reflections on learning, productivity, motivation, and balancing game development with other parts of life.

name: The Spieler
description: Trip Harrison's The Spieler writes critically about game design and interactive narratives, drawing on gaming history and critical theory. The author describes the work as an exploration of games' artistic possibilities and cultural meaning.

name: The Stack
description: Writing about video games from The Stack

name: The Third Player
description: Writing about video games from The Third Player

name: The Video Game Library
description: The Video Game Library documents books about video games, including art books, strategy guides, comics, academic works, and related material. Its newsletter covers new book announcements, additions to the archive, reviews, interviews, and overlooked titles.

name: The Video Game Storyteller
description: The Video Game Storyteller explores stories in video games and the stories games create for players. The publication's stated scope is reflective writing about the narrative and personal significance of games.

name: The XP Drop
description: The XP Drop was a weekly newsletter covering all the essential gaming news, reviews, opinions

name: The blog at the bottom of the sea
description: The blog at the bottom of the sea publishes programming and technical writing on graphics, game development, computation, audio synthesis, and related topics. The author says the posts document implementations and concepts for learning and reference.

name: TheNameBrand
description: TheNameBrand is Brando Calrissian's outlet for video-game reviews and thoughts on the games industry, alongside his YouTube work.

name: TheOtherReviewOutlet’s
description: Have a drink at the crossroads between gaming, culture, and business.

name: Thinky Games
description: Thinky Games helps players discover puzzle and problem-solving games that emphasize reasoning over reflexes. The site curates games, reports on new releases, and maintains a database of thinky titles.

name: This Week in Video Games
description: This Week in Video Games is an independent editorial publication covering curated video-game news, reviews, analysis, and reporting. Its About page describes concise updates and longer-form coverage of games as both a creative medium and an industry.

name: Thrilling Tales of Old Video Games
description: Drew Mackie's Thrilling Tales of Old Video Games explores older games through history, cultural context, lore, and close readings of their stories and design. Recent examples include articles on Metroid history and fantasy creatures in games.

name: Time Extension
description: Time Extension covers news and features about retro and classic games, including interviews, reviews, guides, hardware, and the people and companies behind older systems and games.

name: Timenerf
description: Site no longer exists

name: Toomanywires
description: Toomanywires is a personal video-game blog covering reviews, hands-on impressions, gaming events, and recommendations, with posts spanning current releases and retro games. The feed includes Tokyo Game Show coverage and retrospective categories.

name: Torchlit Gaming
description: Torchlit Gaming is your source for in-depth reviews, editorials, essays, and news on video games, board games, and card games.

name: Umby Cord || Austin on video games
description: Writing about video games from Umby Cord || Austin on video games

name: Updater
description: Updater is journalist Shannon Liao's newsletter for gaming and technology coverage, including industry profiles, founder interviews, company news, layoffs, mergers, unionization, and game previews. Its About page describes follow-up reporting that revisits developing stories.

name: Uppercut
description: Writing about video games from Uppercut

name: Urban Protagonist
description: Site no longer exists

name: VGBees
description: VGBees is a video-game publication and podcast whose feed includes discussions of current games-industry news, releases, and game-related events. Its slogan is 'video games for the hive.'

name: VGPR
description: Writing about video games from VGPR

name: Video Game Deep Cuts
description: Video Game Deep Cuts is Simon Carless's weekly selection of notable articles and videos about video-game culture, including the medium's state, future, and history.

name: Video Game Industry Memo
description: Video Games Industry Memo is George E. Osborn's newsletter explaining the video-game sector through a weekly analysis feature, summarized industry news, job moves, events, and releases.

name: Video Game Stories
description: Welcome to Video Game Stories! Here, you can read unique gaming recommendations, exciting backgrounds about video games, fresh perspectives, and fascinating developer stories

name: Video Games Are Real
description: Writing about video games from Video Games Are Real

name: Video Games Without Borders
description: Writing about video games from Video Games Without Borders

name: Videodante
description: Dante Douglas, known online as videodante, writes about games, narrative, and creative work from the perspective of a writer and game developer. His blog also covers prose and tabletop game work alongside video games.

name: Voletic
description: Voletic is Jordan H.J.'s long-running personal video-game publication, now published through Substack. Its About page recounts earlier custom-site and WordPress phases and explains the author's continued interest in writing about games.

name: Wark Digest from Final Fantasy Union
description: Wark Digest is a weekly Final Fantasy newsletter from the creators of Final Fantasy Union, covering developments in the franchise and reflecting on its history. Related Kupo Chronicle editions provide longer historical deep dives.

name: Wavelengths
description: Wavelengths is Brendon Bigley's personal publication, mixing video-game and technology commentary with other subjects such as recipes. The home page includes gaming hardware coverage, while the About page describes the author's media and entertainment work.

name: World Designer Notebook
description: World Designer Notebook documents its author's processes, problems, and explorations in world design for video games.

name: Yeah Nah Gaming
description: Yeah Nah Gaming is a New Zealand publication for local gamers, with Aotearoa-focused games news and reviews. Its homepage and feed also include technology and culture coverage, including trading-card-game content.

name: jwaaaap
description: jwaaaap is game designer Jan Willem Nijman's occasional newsletter about his work and plans for making games with small teams.

name: nonmateria
description: Writing about video games from nonmateria
